messages:
oncall-bot: :rotating_light: PAGER - Canary routing misrouting detected for service `routing-proxy` (severity: page). Symptoms: spike in 502/504 from canary pool, route TTL mismatch. Trigger: route-ttl-mismatch-alert. Please respond.

maria chen: ack I'm on it, joining logs now. Which canary cluster?

samir patel: seeing elevated 5xx from canary-eu-west-2 (canary pool id: cp-7f3). Samples show backend returned 502 and request headers have `X-Route-TTL: -1` in a few traces.

leo ng: adding context — we rolled out the new route cache ff yesterday: `ff:new-route-cache` enabled for 10% canary traffic at 09:12 UTC.

deploy-bot: Deploy note: canary rollout `routing-proxy:v2.3.0` started 2026-03-15T09:12:21Z (triggered by pipeline #4821). Feature flag `new-route-cache` = true for canary.

maria chen: ok, priority first: disable the ff for canary immediately. Samir, can you confirm the ff service command?

samir patel: run `curl -XPOST https://ff-service/api/v1/flags/new-route-cache/disable -d '{"scope":"canary"}'` or use `ffctl toggle new-route-cache --scope=canary --off`.

jordan li: i'm pushing the toggle now. `ffctl toggle new-route-cache --scope=canary --off` -> returned 200.

maria chen: checking metrics... still some errors but lower than before. The X-Route-TTL header in new traces is back to expected positive ints. Might be sticky sessions to nodes that had corrupted TTL.

sre-ops: we have a small set of sessions pinned to old canary instances with bad KV state. Warm draining those pods might help. Recommend rolling back the canary image to v2.2.4 while we verify cache integrity.

leo ng: agree. Rolling back will be faster than hunting per-session fixes. I'll start the rollback unless there's objection.

samir patel: roll it. Command: `kubectl -n prod set image deployment/routing-proxy routing-proxy=registry.redwood/v2.2.4 --record` then `kubectl rollout status deploy/routing-proxy`.

maria chen: initiating rollback now. Pasting command output: ```
kubectl set image deployment/routing-proxy routing-proxy=registry.redwood/v2.2.4
deployment.apps/routing-proxy image updated
Waiting for rollout to finish: 1 of 5 updated...
Rollout completed successfully
```

oncall-bot: Auto-check: post-rollback error rate dropped to baseline (~0.3%). Canary pool health: OK. Route TTL mismatch alerts cleared.

cs-ops: CS: we saw ~6 requests from 2 merchants fail with retries around 09:15-09:18 UTC. No broad customer outage but a few payment failures were reported — filing incident for CS follow-up.

jordan li: noted. I'll attach a short blameless summary for CS: cause - route cache/TTL edge-case during canary causing session pinning to stale instances. Mitigation - ff toggle + rollback to v2.2.4 + pod drain.

leo ng: created runbook note: add aggressive cache sanity checks post-deploy and a canary health gate for `X-Route-TTL` header sanity within the first 5 minutes.

maria chen: thanks. I'm going to run the post-mortem checklist and add action items: 1) add automated TTL sanity check to canary probe, 2) expand canary traffic shard to include synthetic users exercising sticky sessions, 3) investigate race in route cache write path.

sre-ops: handoff: i'll stay during the immediate cool-down for 10 more minutes, then hand to night oncall. Next oncall is `jordan li` at 10:00 UTC.

maria chen: summary for handoff -> Root cause likely bug in `new-route-cache` where negative TTL values were occasionally written on cache rebuild, causing proxy to forward to stale canary pods. Customer impact limited (few payments failed), mitigations executed: ff toggle, rollback, pod drain. Monitoring: error-rate and `X-Route-TTL` sanity. Links: logs and dashboard -> https://grafana.redwood/board/routing-proxy-canary, runbook -> https://confluence.redwood/runbooks/canary-deploys.

jordan li: taking over the oncall here, will monitor metrics for next 2 hours and own follow-ups. If anything degrades I'll escalate. :thumbsup:

maria chen: thanks all, closing pager. Please add any additional notes to the incident thread if you spot follow-on issues.
